Also, I would like to have a current accuracy rate of the pipeline on that dashboard. Write ma a plan/overview I can feed into the Claude Design AI to generate the design. Think of all of the useful info for pipeline developers to see.

1	---
2	name: fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular
3	description: "fight-ai round \"ground truth\" spans are auto-seeded from the pipeline's own AI output, so scoring round IoU against them is circular"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 579b1254-323f-42d1-b482-42c5ad365f5c
8	---
9	
10	`backend/app/services/label_span_service.py:10-34` seeds `label_spans` of kind
11	`round` from the `rounds` table (AI segmentation output) the first time the
12	Annotate page requests them, so the labeller starts pre-filled. If nobody edits
13	them, the "ground truth" is byte-identical to the prediction.
14	
15	As of 2026-08-17 that was true of fight 46 (DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA) — 3 spans, one
16	shared microsecond-identical `created_at`, `labeled_at` NULL, 0 strike events,
17	and `segmentation_needs_review = true` with a reason calling the boundaries
18	"a guess". Fight 42 also matched AI output exactly; only fight 44 had a
19	human-adjusted round start.
20	
21	**Why:** scoring round IoU against seeded spans reads 1.000 before any change
22	and makes every genuine segmentation *improvement* look like a regression.
23	
24	**How to apply:** before trusting a round-IoU number, check whether the label
25	span differs from the `rounds` row and whether the span timestamps are
26	distinct. `eval.cli export` refuses fights with `labeled_at IS NULL`, which
27	catches the unfinished case but *not* the seeded-then-finished case.
28	Also note 3 of 4 fights were processed on the manual-labeling track and have
29	zero `fight_events`, so strike P/R/F1 is structurally 0 for them.
30	See [[easyocr-confidence-is-noise]].

1	---
2	name: corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground
3	description: "eval/corner_accuracy.py reads the shorts band as a fraction of bbox height, so it goes nearly blind on ground/clinch frames — a low decisive-frame count is \"unverified\", not \"fine\""
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: reference
7	  originSessionId: 53047172-e54e-4eb1-a0f1-31064b2e9209
8	  modified: 2026-08-23T07:32:54.047Z
9	---
10	
11	`ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py` samples each fighter's shorts band at
12	`_BAND_TOP=0.42` to `_BAND_BOTTOM=0.72` **of bbox height**. That geometry only
13	lands on the trunks when the fighter is upright. On the ground the bbox goes
14	wide-and-short and the band slices across arms, canvas and the opponent, so
15	`_colour_vote` almost never clears `_MIN_COLOUR_PX` / `_MIN_DECISIVENESS`.
16	
17	Measured 2026-08-23 on DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA (a ground-heavy fight, 83 of 163 hand
18	labels are `ground_punch`), frames 1199–34767 at stride 15 (~2200 frames
19	sampled):
20	
21	- fight 48 (old pipeline): **7** decisive frames
22	- fight 52 (new pipeline): **3** decisive frames
23	
24	Whole-fight at stride 10 the same fight yields 55 decisive frames — i.e. the
25	evidence comes almost entirely from the standing portions elsewhere in the video.
26	
27	**Why:** a whole-fight accuracy number is therefore not evenly distributed over
28	the fight. It can read "56% correct" while contributing essentially zero
29	evidence about the ground exchanges, which is exactly where tracker identity
30	swaps are most likely and where corner errors do the most damage to training
31	data.
32	
33	**How to apply:** treat a low decisive-frame count as *unverified*, never as a
34	pass — the module's own docstring says this for the zero case and the same
35	applies at n=3. For ground-heavy footage, verify corners by eye
36	(`--verify-pose` overlay video) or via labeller-marked `corner_swap` spans
37	rather than trusting this number. Also note `format_accuracy` only prints runs
38	of >= 3 frames (`min_run`), so short flapping runs are invisible in its output —
39	count runs, not just accuracy, to see instability. Related:
40	[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]], [[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].
41

1	---
2	name: label-events-corner-is-box-not-person
3	description: "Filip labels strikes by the overlay box, not the named fighter, so label_events.corner is a track-slot pointer — the planned corner_swap flip at export would corrupt training data rather than fix it"
4	metadata:
5	  type: project
6	---
7	
8	Stated by Filip 2026-08-31. When the overlay shows a corner swap (Roy carrying
9	the red box), he selects **red** and logs the punch — i.e. he picks the
10	rectangle around the fighter who threw it, not the fighter named red at upload.
11	
12	So `label_events.corner` and `fighter_frames.corner` are **the same pointer**:
13	both name a track slot, not a person. Inside a `corner_swap` span they are both
14	"wrong" about the name and consistent about the human. The Stage 2 join
15	`label_events(F, corner) -> fighter_frames(F, corner) -> keypoints` therefore
16	already yields correct training rows with nothing applied.
17	
18	**Why:** it inverts the design in the plan. Applying the swap at export — as
19	`ai/eval/schema.py:152` ("Applied at export time when joining labels to
20	fighter_frames.keypoints") and `plan/02c-labelling-ui.md:156` ("flips red/blue
21	in the exported training tensor") both instruct — would attach the label to the
22	*other* fighter's skeleton. That is the exact silent corruption
23	`plan/02a-upload-tracks.md:95` set out to prevent, caused by the mitigation.
24	The premise there was identity-labelling; the actual convention is
25	box-labelling, under which the corruption never existed.
26	
27	**How to apply:** never apply `corner_swaps` to a label-to-keypoint join. Apply
28	it only where a *person* is needed (per-fighter stats, `fight_events.fighter_id`),
29	and at read time — mutating `fighter_frames.corner` would desync it from
30	`label_events.corner` and break the join that currently works. Two knock-ons:
31	`score.py:225`'s "fighter attribution %" is circular (the labeller read the
32	corner off the pipeline's own overlay, so it can never detect a swap — cf.
33	[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]]); and span *boundary* error no longer
34	corrupts training data as `plan/02d-label-quality.md:213` claims, though
35	detection rate still matters for the tracker metric. The spans remain the
36	ground truth for [[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]], which is now their
37	main purpose. See also [[corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground]].
38

1	---
2	name: tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches
3	description: Identity swaps enter at camera switches and clinches; the hand-labelled corner_swap spans are the ground truth for measuring them.
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fbf2c258-92a1-4a58-8ba1-d5ff99286f32
8	  modified: 2026-08-30T09:58:26.350Z

10	
11	Measured 2026-08-30 against the labeller's own `label_spans` of kind
12	`corner_swap` — these are the ground truth for identity swaps and need no
13	re-run to use. Fight 54 has 8 spans (6–35 s each), fight 52 has 5 (1.7–8.7 s).
14	
15	Against a 5000-frame random control per fight, window ±6 frames:
16	- **fight 54 span STARTS**: 4/8 in the top decile of frame-to-frame box jump
17	  (chance 1.5) — a camera switch.
18	- **fight 54 span ENDS**: 4/7 in the top decile of inter-fighter box IoU
19	  (chance 1.5).
20	- **fight 52 span STARTS**: median inter-fighter IoU 0.73 vs control 0.00 — a
21	  clinch.
22	
23	Both entry points are where `FighterTracker`'s geometry-only cost is
24	uninformative. n is small (5 and 8 spans), so treat this as directional.
25	
26	Two structural facts behind it: nothing in `ai/` detects a shot boundary at all
27	(grep for cut/shot/scene finds only prose), and `FighterTracker._assign` has **no
28	maximum-cost gate** — only the Hungarian padding cells carry the 1e6 sentinel, so
29	a detection anywhere in the frame will always match some slot rather than letting
30	the slot coast.
31	
32	A global HSV-histogram cut detector is the wrong instrument here: it found only
33	29 cuts in 47k frames of fight 54, because broadcast MMA cuts between cameras
34	pointed at the same cage barely change the global histogram. Use the geometric
35	signal (simultaneous box jump) instead.
36	
37	**Why:** a swap that enters at a cut persists until the next one, because
38	`assign_corners` can only apply a global flip — see
39	[[corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps]].
40	
41	**How to apply:** measure any tracking change against these spans rather than by
42	eye, and check the run log first — on fight 54 the appearance path was skipped
43	entirely (`ambiguous tape (both slots read blue)`), so the static legacy map ran
44	and no swap was corrected at all.

1	---
2	name: corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps
3	description: "assign_corners' hysteresis barrier is charged twice, so a tracker identity swap is mathematically uncorrectable without visible glove tape."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fbf2c258-92a1-4a58-8ba1-d5ff99286f32
8	  modified: 2026-08-30T09:58:15.667Z
9	---
10	
11	Measured 2026-08-30. In `assign_corners._assign_frame_labels`, `_cost` adds
12	`CORNER_HYSTERESIS_WEIGHT` (0.5) per detection whose label would flip. A corner
13	swap always flips both slots, so the barrier is **1.0**. Evidence per detection
14	is `CORNER_TAPE_WEIGHT` (0.6) × tape + `CORNER_HIST_WEIGHT` (0.4) × hist, and
15	when no glove tape is visible `_tape_distance_term` returns exactly 0.5 for both
16	corners (confidence factor 0), so the tape term cancels. Torso histogram alone
17	can therefore move the two-detection total by at most **0.8 < 1.0**: the flip
18	can never win. In practice Bhattacharyya gaps give ~0.16–0.32, versus a 1.0
19	barrier.
20	
21	The single-detection branch charges the barrier only **once** (0.5), so a
22	one-sided observation faces a *lower* bar than both fighters seen together —
23	backwards, since it is the weaker evidence.
24	
25	**Why:** this is the only mechanism that can repair a `FighterTracker` identity
26	swap, and it is disabled exactly when the gloves aren't visible — which is most
27	of a clinch and most of a ground sequence.
28	
29	**How to apply:** charge the barrier once per *mapping* decision (it is a
30	bijection — see the atomic-commit note already in ai/CLAUDE.md), consistently in
31	both branches, before touching the constant's value. Note the deeper issue too:
32	the mapping is global, so it cannot represent a swap that lasts only from one
33	camera cut to the next, and the run logs show it flip-flopping 444–813 times per
34	fight chasing local errors with a global boolean. See
35	[[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]] and
36	[[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].
37

10	Measured 2026-08-17 on `DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA.mp4`: re-OCRing the *same* scoreboard
11	digits under a ≤1px change to the calibrated ROI moves EasyOCR's line
12	confidence by a **median of 0.117, max 0.433**. 30% of correct timer readings
13	straddle 0.7. So `SCOREBOARD_OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE` gates on a quantity noisier
14	than any increment worth tuning, and there is a feedback loop: calibration only
15	unions boxes clearing the floor, so changing the floor changes the ROI, which
16	changes the confidences again.
17	
18	**Why:** it means "tune the OCR confidence threshold" is never the right
19	framing for a scoreboard-coverage problem — the number is not measuring
20	reading quality. What actually rejects bad reads is structural: the
21	seconds>59/minutes>59 range check in `parsers.py` and the clock-intercept fit
22	in `fight_segmentation.py`.
23	
24	**How to apply:** to check whether a timer read is real, don't look at
25	confidence — compute `k = frame/fps + seconds_remaining` and test whether it
26	agrees with the round's intercept. Real reads cluster within ~0.5s (the 2 Hz
27	sampling quantum); misreads land far off. This is a label-free correctness
28	check and is how the 0.7→0.5 change was validated over 4781 samples with zero
29	false reads. See [[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]].

1	# Evaluation harness
2	
3	Measurement layer for the processing pipeline. Nothing here is imported by the
4	pipeline — it only reads what the pipeline persisted to PostgreSQL and compares
5	it against hand-labelled ground truth.
6	
7	It exists because the pipeline currently has ~40 hand-tuned constants in
8	`models/constants.py` and no way to tell whether changing one helps. Every
9	tuning decision so far was made by eyeballing a single video. That does not
10	converge: a threshold that fixes one clip silently breaks another, and there is
11	no signal to say so.
12	
13	## Quick start
14	
15	Labelling itself happens in the frontend, not here — upload a video in
16	**manual** mode, open it in the Annotate page, and use the on-screen palette
17	(see its own keyboard legend). This harness is where a finished labelling
18	session becomes ground truth on disk and gets scored against.
19	
20	```bash
21	cd ai
22	
23	# 0. Check the source video decodes fully — do this FIRST, see below
24	python -m eval.cli video fight_videos/BATURvsSTAMATOVIC.mp4
25	
26	# 1. Once the fight is fully labelled and "Finish Labeling" was clicked,
27	#    build eval/labels/<video>.json from label_events/label_spans in Postgres
28	python -m eval.cli export fight_videos/BATURvsSTAMATOVIC.mp4
29	
30	# 2. Check pipeline output for impossible artifacts — needs no labels
31	python -m eval.cli sanity fight_videos/BATURvsSTAMATOVIC.mp4
32	
33	# 3. Score the pipeline against ground truth
34	python -m eval.cli score fight_videos/BATURvsSTAMATOVIC.mp4
35	
36	# 4. Track labelling progress
37	python -m eval.cli summary
38	```
39	
40	Labels live in `eval/labels/<video_stem>.json` and **are committed to git** —
41	they are expensive hand work and the single most valuable artifact in the repo.
42	`export` refuses to run against a fight that hasn't been through "Finish
43	Labeling" (`labeled_at IS NULL`) — that's the only durable marker that a
44	fight's ground truth is actually finished, since `state` gets reset the
45	moment a labelled fight is re-run through the AI pipeline to become an
46	evaluation fixture.
47	
48	## Check the video first
49	
50	`python -m eval.cli video <path>` decodes the whole file and compares the result
51	against the container's advertised frame count. A truncated download opens
52	fine, reports a full duration, and simply stops decoding partway through — the
53	pipeline processes the decodable prefix and reports success.
54	
55	The only video currently in `fight_videos/` is in exactly this state:
56	
57	```
58	container reports   24712 frames  (8.2 min)
59	decoder yields       8147 frames  (2.7 min)
60	[FAIL] TRUNCATED — 16565 frames (67%) never decode.
61	```
62	
63	**Every threshold in `models/constants.py` was tuned against the first third of
64	one broken fight**, with corrupt frames around the break feeding the pose model.
65	Re-download before drawing conclusions from any metric.
66	
67	## Start with `sanity`
68	
69	The sanity checks need no labels and catch output that is *internally
70	impossible* rather than merely inaccurate. They will tell you more, faster,
71	than an F1 score will. On the current pipeline, four of six fail:
72	
73	```
74	[FAIL] events inside rounds        75/94 strikes fall outside every detected round
75	[FAIL] no simultaneous mutual strikes   30 frames have BOTH fighters striking
76	[FAIL] state does not flap         55 transitions over 1.1 min = 50.0/min
77	[FAIL] state dwell is physical     median 0.62s between state changes
78	```
79	
80	Two fighters do not throw punches on the same frame 30 times in a fight, and
81	fight state does not alternate every 0.6 seconds. These are bugs with specific
82	causes, not thresholds that need nudging.
83	
84	## Then run `corner_accuracy` — before you label anything
85	
86	```
87	python -m eval.corner_accuracy <fight_id>
88	```
89	
90	Also label-free. It reads `fighter_frames.corner` back and checks it against
91	each fighter's kit colour, because a red/blue inversion is the one error that
92	leaves every artifact perfectly self-consistent: `sanity` sees valid structure,
93	`score` needs labels, and the labels themselves inherit the error the moment a
94	human starts tagging against a wrong overlay. Two of three fights were wrong
95	when this check was written:
96	
97	```
98	fight 31  JURICvsNOGUEIRA        100%  OK
99	fight 42  MILIDRAGOVICvsMOOSMAN    1%  [FAIL]  whole fight inverted
100	fight 44  NAZHANDvsSTAROPOLI      66%  [WARN]  intermittent tracker swaps
101	```
102	
103	`[FAIL]` means the whole-fight mapping is backwards. `[WARN]` means the
104	appearance path failed to correct tracker identity swaps — the FLIPPED frame
105	ranges it prints are where `corner_swap` spans belong. **"No decisive frames"
106	is not a pass**; it means the kit colours never read unambiguously and corner
107	assignment is simply unverified for that fight.
108	
109	Run this before labelling. Labels recorded against an inverted overlay are
110	attributed to the wrong fighter and are silently useless as training data.
111	
112	## Labelling guide
113	
114	Labelling happens in the Annotate page (upload in **manual** mode, wait for
115	`LABELING_IN_PROGRESS`, open the fight). The palette and its keyboard
116	shortcuts are self-documenting via the on-page keyboard legend; the
117	conventions below are the ones that aren't obvious from the UI alone. The
118	labels are also the training set for the skeleton action model, so
119	consistency matters more than volume.
120	
121	**Which frame to mark.** The frame of impact, or of peak extension for a
122	strike that misses. The scorer uses a ±0.25s window by default, so being a
123	frame or two off is harmless — being systematically early or late is not.
124	
125	**Log every strike thrown, outcome unknown.** Landed-vs-missed is deferred —
126	every strike is recorded with `success = null`. The model needs negatives too,
127	so a punch that visibly misses still gets logged, not skipped.
128	
129	**Red vs. blue means the box on screen, not the name.** Select the corner whose
130	rectangle is currently drawn around the fighter who acted, even when the overlay
131	has them swapped: if red is on Roy right now and Roy punches, select **red**.
132	This keeps your label and the persisted skeleton pointing at the same human, so
133	the training join is correct with no correction applied — and so a swap span
134	whose edge is a few frames off costs nothing.
135	
136	**And mark the swap anyway.** When the overlay shows a swapped corner (most
137	likely mid-clinch), open a `corner_swap` span over it (`O` to open, `O` again to
138	close) — never `excluded`, those are exactly the frames the model most needs.
139	The span is not a fix to your labels; it is the ground truth for how often
140	corner assignment fails, which is one of the things being measured, and the
141	slot → person map for per-fighter statistics.
142	
143	**Exclude mid-round replays and camera cuts** with an `excluded` span (`P` to
144	open, `P` again to close). Excluded spans are dropped from every metric, so a
145	predicted event inside one is neither a hit nor a false positive. Slow-motion
146	replays especially must be excluded: velocity thresholds are meaningless
147	there. Between-round rest and pre/post-fight footage don't need this — they're
148	already outside every `round` span.
149	
150	**Round bounds** are seeded from AI segmentation and shown as a draggable span
151	in the ROUNDS lane — confirm or nudge the edges rather than re-marking from
152	scratch. Everything outside a round is not training data and not scored.
153	"Finish Labeling" requires every detected round to have a confirmed span.
154	
155	**State marks** (`W`/`F`/`G` for STRIKING/CLINCH/GROUND) are change points, not
156	spans — mark the frame where the state genuinely changes and the span is
157	derived automatically, running to the next mark (or the end of the round for
158	the last one).
159	
160	**Elbows** have no pipeline equivalent yet. Label them anyway — they will score
161	as false negatives, which is the honest reading, and the action model will
162	need them.
163	
164	## Reading the score report
165	
166	**Strike detection** is matched with optimal (Hungarian) assignment on temporal
167	distance, not greedy nearest-match, so the score does not depend on which end of
168	the video you start from.
169	
170	Matching **ignores the fighter** by default, and attribution accuracy is
171	reported separately. This is deliberate: "we missed the strike" and "we saw the
172	strike but credited the wrong corner" are different bugs with different fixes,
173	and a joint match key would hide detection progress behind corner-assignment
174	noise. Pass `--strict-fighter` to fold it back in.
175	
176	**Non-specific predictions are excluded from the family/target denominators.**
177	The pipeline emits `clinch_punch` / `ground_punch` with no punch family and no
178	target zone, so grading those against a labelled `hook`/`head` would penalise it
179	for a distinction it never attempts. They still count for detection.
180	
181	**Only scored frames count** — inside a labelled round and outside every
182	excluded span. Events on either side are dropped rather than counted as false
183	positives.
184	
185	For fight state, watch `transitions/min` and `median dwell` more than per-frame
186	accuracy. Per-frame accuracy is dominated by whichever state is most common and
187	stays high even when the state machine is visibly flapping.
188	
189	## How many labels?
190	
191	~300 strikes is the working target before the skeleton action model can be
192	expected to beat hand-tuned rules — roughly 10–15 minutes of round time. Two or
193	three fights. `python -m eval.cli summary` tracks progress toward it.
194	
195	For evaluation alone, far fewer are useful: even 50 labelled strikes on one
196	round will tell you whether a change to `constants.py` helped or hurt, which is
197	strictly more than is knowable today.
198	
199	## Before labelling at volume: measure the labels themselves
200	
201	Every number above is measured against hand labels treated as ground truth.
202	Nothing measures the labels themselves unless you run these — do it on the
203	*first* labelled fight, not the last, since the disagreement list doubles as a
204	review queue that catches an underspecified taxonomy before 300 strikes are
205	committed to it.
206	
207	**Double-labelling ceiling.** Label one round twice — ideally a second
208	person, or the same labeller with a week's gap so they don't just remember and
209	agree with themselves — and measure how much the two passes agree:
210	
211	```bash
212	python -m eval.cli export fight_videos/x.mp4                # primary pass
213	python -m eval.cli export fight_videos/x.mp4 --as alex       # second pass → x.alex.json
214	python -m eval.cli agreement fight_videos/x.mp4              # writes x.agreement.json
215	```
216	
217	Reports **F1 only** — `score()` is asymmetric (truth vs. on-trial) and between
218	two humans there is no truth, so precision/recall trade places if you swap the
219	passes while F1 stays fixed; F1 is the only claim that doesn't silently assert
220	who was right. Once `x.agreement.json` exists, `score` prints it beside every
221	subsequent F1 for that video as a ceiling — a tuned setting that scores above
222	it is fitting label noise, not detecting strikes better than a human would.
223	
224	**Matching tolerance is pinned, not a free dial.** `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS` in
225	`score.py` is the single source of truth; `--tolerance-override` on `score` /
226	`agreement` warns loudly when used and should come with a reason recorded
227	somewhere. The report also separates **bias** (median signed offset — a
228	systematic lag, e.g. labeller reaction time) from **jitter** (median absolute
229	offset — genuine spread): a bias is a constant to subtract once, not a reason
230	to widen the tolerance window.
231	
232	**Corner-swap recall.** `0a`'s mitigation for corner-assignment errors is that
233	the labeller *sees* a swap on the overlay and marks it — untested, and applied
234	to the hardest place on screen to notice anything (overlapping boxes
235	mid-clinch). Measure it before relying on it at volume:
236	
237	```bash
238	python -m eval.cli inject-swap fight_videos/x.mp4 --start 3200 --end 3450
239	# label the fight normally, including the injected window, then:
240	python -m eval.cli export fight_videos/x.mp4
241	python -m eval.cli corner-swap-recall fight_videos/x.mp4 --start 3200 --end 3450
242	# UPDATE ... SET corner = 1 - corner is its own inverse:
243	python -m eval.cli inject-swap fight_videos/x.mp4 --start 3200 --end 3450   # restores
244	```
245	
246	Detection is the number that matters. Boundary error in frames per edge is worth
247	recording but is *not* a training-data risk: labels are logged against the box,
248	so a span that starts 30 frames late still exports 30 correct frames — the edge
249	only shifts per-fighter attribution. Until this has been run and passed, "fraction of
250	labelled frames covered by a `corner_swap` span" is a **lower bound** on the
251	pipeline's corner-assignment error rate, not the real figure — report it as
252	one.
253	
254	**Not yet built:** persisting `assign_corners()`'s own per-frame confidence
255	margin and pre-highlighting the marginal spans for review, so the labeller
256	scans a short candidate queue instead of 8,000 frames. The recall test above
257	works without it; it would make the mitigation itself cheaper to apply
258	correctly. Worth doing once the recall numbers say it's needed.
259	
260	## Known gap
261	
262	`fight_events.state` is now the structured source of truth for a
263	STRIKING/CLINCH/GROUND transition row (`predictions.py` reads it directly);
264	the free-text regex over `description` survives only as a fallback for rows
265	written before that column existed.
266	
267	## Stage 1 finding: fixing the pose-sharing bug collapsed grappling detection
268	
269	After landing Stage 1 steps 1–5 and 7 (Hungarian pose↔detection assignment,
270	confidence-gated geometry, round gating, scale-relative thresholds,
271	fps-invariant timing, temporal state smoothing — see `plan/03-stage1-artifacts.md`),
272	a full re-run on `JURICvsNOGUEIRA.mp4` fixed `no simultaneous mutual strikes`
273	and `no duplicate events` (both now PASS) but dropped `state does not flap`'s
274	input to zero transitions and cut total strikes from 93 to 7 — `strike rate
275	plausible` now FAILs low (3.1/min vs. the expected 5–60).
276	
277	**This is very likely the pose-sharing bug's true effect being removed, not a
278	new regression.** Before step 1, red and blue could be assigned the *same*
279	pose skeleton, making torso-rect distance read exactly 0 — which reads as
280	maximally entangled. That is almost certainly what was driving the baseline's
281	27 `clinch_punch` + assorted ground events and its 44 state transitions in
282	2.3 minutes (55/min — already flagged as unrealistic flapping, not a real
283	state). With one-to-one assignment, real torso-rect separation is measured,
284	and a direct query against this run's `fighter_frames` shows only ~2% of
285	both-fighters-confident frames read as entangled at the current
286	`DISTANCE_GRAPPLING_RATIO` (0.11) — too sparse to ever hold the
287	`FIGHT_STATE_SMOOTHING_WINDOW_SECS`/`FIGHT_STATE_MIN_DWELL_SECS` window, so
288	the state machine never leaves its initial STRIKING seed and every
289	clinch/ground strike type becomes unreachable for this fight.
290	
291	`DISTANCE_GRAPPLING_RATIO` (and the other new `_RATIO`/`_SECS` constants from
292	step 4/5) were calibrated by preserving the *old absolute-pixel threshold's*
293	apparent behaviour against this video's median torso scale — a reasonable
294	placeholder with no ground truth to do better, but not a real calibration.
295	**Do not hand-tune it further by eyeballing this one video** — that is
296	exactly the anti-pattern this whole harness exists to replace. This is
297	precisely what Stage 1 step 8 (the threshold sweep, blocked on Stage 0
298	labels) exists to fix properly. Baseline artifact:
299	`eval/baselines/JURICvsNOGUEIRA-stage1-partial.json`.

1	"""Ground-truth label format for fight videos.
2	
3	One JSON file per video, stored in ``eval/labels/<video_stem>.json``. The format
4	serves double duty: it is the evaluation ground truth *and* the training set for
5	the skeleton action model that will replace the rule cascade, so strike
6	attributes are stored decomposed (family / target / landed) rather than as the
7	pipeline's flat ``jab_head`` strings.
8	
9	Frames are **1-based**, matching the pipeline's frame-numbering contract
10	(see ai/CLAUDE.md — the Nth frame of the video is frame N).
11	
12	Schema
13	------
14	```json
15	{
16	  "video":      "BATURvsSTAMATOVIC.mp4",
17	  "fps":        50,
18	  "frame_count": 8147,
19	  "labeler":    "filip",
20	  "labeled_at": "2026-08-06",
21	  "notes":      "free text",
22	  "rounds":   [{"round": 1, "start": 1507, "end": 4809}],
23	  "excluded": [{"start": 4810, "end": 5200, "reason": "replay"}],
24	  "states":   [{"start": 1507, "end": 1600, "state": "STRIKING"}],
25	  "strikes":  [{"frame": 1620, "fighter": "red", "family": "jab",
26	                "target": "head", "landed": true}]
27	}
28	```
29	
30	``excluded`` regions (replays, walkouts, corner rest, camera cuts) are dropped
31	from every metric — both a predicted and a ground-truth event inside one is
32	ignored rather than counted as a false positive.
33	"""
34	
35	import json
36	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
37	from pathlib import Path
38	from typing import Optional
39	
40	LABELS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "labels"
41	
42	# --- Taxonomy -------------------------------------------------------------
43	# Strike families. `punch` is the deliberately unspecific bucket the pipeline
44	# emits in clinch/ground (clinch_punch / ground_punch) where it does not attempt
45	# a jab/cross/hook/uppercut split. Labellers should always use a specific family;
46	# `punch` exists so predictions can be represented faithfully.
47	FAMILIES = ("jab", "cross", "hook", "uppercut", "elbow", "knee", "kick", "punch")
48	SPECIFIC_FAMILIES = ("jab", "cross", "hook", "uppercut", "elbow", "knee", "kick")
49	
50	# Target zones. `unknown` is again a prediction-only value: the pipeline's
51	# grappling strikes carry no target.
52	TARGETS = ("head", "body", "leg", "unknown")
53	
54	FIGHTERS = ("red", "blue")
55	STATES = ("STRIKING", "CLINCH", "GROUND")
56	
57	# --- Pipeline vocabulary → (family, target) -------------------------------
58	# Maps the flat `fight_events.action` strings the pipeline writes onto the
59	# decomposed label taxonomy, so predictions and ground truth are comparable.
60	PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
61	    "jab_head":      ("jab",      "head"),
62	    "jab_body":      ("jab",      "body"),
63	    "cross_head":    ("cross",    "head"),
64	    "cross_body":    ("cross",    "body"),
65	    "hook_head":     ("hook",     "head"),
66	    "hook_body":     ("hook",     "body"),
67	    "uppercut_head": ("uppercut", "head"),
68	    "uppercut_body": ("uppercut", "body"),
69	    "head_kick":     ("kick",     "head"),
70	    "middle_kick":   ("kick",     "body"),
71	    "low_kick":      ("kick",     "leg"),
72	    # Grappling strikes carry neither a punch family nor a target zone.
73	    "clinch_punch":  ("punch",    "unknown"),
74	    "ground_punch":  ("punch",    "unknown"),
75	    "clinch_knee":   ("knee",     "unknown"),
76	    "ground_knee":   ("knee",     "unknown"),
77	}
78	
79	# Non-strike `action` values written to fight_events.
80	STATE_ACTIONS = {"round_start", "round_end", "clinch_initiated", "takedown_initiated"}
81	
82	
83	class LabelError(ValueError):
84	    """Raised when a label file fails validation."""
85	
86	
87	@dataclass
88	class Strike:
89	    frame: int
90	    fighter: str          # red | blue
91	    family: str           # see FAMILIES
92	    target: str           # see TARGETS
93	    landed: Optional[bool] = None
94	
95	    @property
96	    def is_specific(self) -> bool:
97	        """True when family and target are both committed values.
98	
99	        Grappling predictions are non-specific; they still count for
100	        event-level detection but are excluded from the family/target accuracy
101	        denominators so the pipeline is not penalised for a distinction it does
102	        not attempt to make.
103	        """
104	        return self.family in SPECIFIC_FAMILIES and self.target != "unknown"
105	
106	
107	@dataclass
108	class Takedown:
109	    frame: int
110	    fighter: str          # red | blue — the fighter who landed it
111	
112	
113	@dataclass
114	class Span:
115	    start: int
116	    end: int
117	
118	    def contains(self, frame: int) -> bool:
119	        return self.start <= frame <= self.end
120	
121	    @property
122	    def length(self) -> int:
123	        return max(0, self.end - self.start + 1)
124	
125	
126	@dataclass
127	class Round(Span):
128	    round: int = 1
129	
130	
131	@dataclass
132	class Excluded(Span):
133	    reason: str = ""
134	
135	
136	@dataclass
137	class StateSpan(Span):
138	    state: str = "STRIKING"
139	
140	
141	@dataclass
142	class FightLabels:
143	    video: str
144	    fps: int
145	    frame_count: int = 0
146	    labeler: str = ""
147	    labeled_at: str = ""
148	    notes: str = ""
149	    rounds: list[Round] = field(default_factory=list)
150	    excluded: list[Excluded] = field(default_factory=list)
151	    states: list[StateSpan] = field(default_factory=list)
152	    strikes: list[Strike] = field(default_factory=list)
153	    # Labeller-marked "red/blue are flipped here" stretches (see 0a/0d in the
154	    # plan) — corner_assignment's known failure mode.
155	    #
156	    # **Do NOT apply these to a label->keypoint join.** `corner` is a track-slot
157	    # pointer, not a person: the labeller selects a corner by clicking the *box*
158	    # the overlay draws, so inside a swap span `label_events.corner` and
159	    # `fighter_frames.corner` are consistently "wrong" about the name and
160	    # correct about the human. The Stage 2 join label_events(F, corner) ->
161	    # fighter_frames(F, corner) -> keypoints therefore already lands on the
162	    # skeleton that threw the strike, with nothing applied; flipping here would
163	    # attach the label to the *other* fighter.
164	    #
165	    # These spans are (a) the slot->person map — apply only where a person is
166	    # required, e.g. per-fighter stats and fight_events.fighter_id — and (b) the
167	    # ground truth for tracker identity swaps (see corner_swap_check).
168	    # fighter_frames is never mutated either way.
169	    corner_swaps: list[Span] = field(default_factory=list)
170	    # Landed takedowns only (`takedown_landed` in the palette) — `fighter` is
171	    # unambiguous (the one who landed it). `takedown_attempt`/`_defended` are
172	    # NOT captured here: `takedown_defended` logs the *defender* as `fighter`,
173	    # not the attacker, so unifying all three into one outcome-tagged list
174	    # needs its own design decision, not made here. Not yet scored against
175	    # the pipeline's `takedown_initiated` predictions — captured so the data
176	    # isn't silently dropped, scoring is a follow-up.
177	    takedowns: list[Takedown] = field(default_factory=list)
178	
179	    # -- exclusion / round helpers ----------------------------------------
180	
181	    def is_excluded(self, frame: int) -> bool:
182	        return any(e.contains(frame) for e in self.excluded)
183	
184	    def in_any_round(self, frame: int) -> bool:
185	        return any(r.contains(frame) for r in self.rounds)
186	
187	    def scored_frames(self) -> set[int]:
188	        """Frames eligible for scoring: inside a round and not excluded.
189	
190	        When no rounds are labelled, every non-excluded frame up to
191	        ``frame_count`` is eligible — this lets a partially-labelled file still
192	        produce numbers.
193	        """
194	        if self.rounds:
195	            candidate = {f for r in self.rounds for f in range(r.start, r.end + 1)}
196	        else:
197	            candidate = set(range(1, self.frame_count + 1))
198	        return {f for f in candidate if not self.is_excluded(f)}
199	
200	    def state_at(self, frame: int) -> Optional[str]:
201	        for s in self.states:
202	            if s.contains(frame):
203	                return s.state
204	        return None
205	
206	    # -- persistence -------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    @classmethod
209	    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "FightLabels":
210	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
211	            raw = json.load(f)
212	        labels = cls(
213	            video=raw["video"],
214	            fps=int(raw["fps"]),
215	            frame_count=int(raw.get("frame_count", 0)),
216	            labeler=raw.get("labeler", ""),
217	            labeled_at=raw.get("labeled_at", ""),
218	            notes=raw.get("notes", ""),
219	            rounds=[Round(**r) for r in raw.get("rounds", [])],
220	            excluded=[Excluded(**e) for e in raw.get("excluded", [])],
221	            states=[StateSpan(**s) for s in raw.get("states", [])],
222	            strikes=[Strike(**s) for s in raw.get("strikes", [])],
223	            corner_swaps=[Span(**c) for c in raw.get("corner_swaps", [])],
224	            takedowns=[Takedown(**t) for t in raw.get("takedowns", [])],
225	        )
226	        labels.validate()
227	        return labels
228	
229	    @classmethod
230	    def for_video(cls, video: str | Path) -> "FightLabels":
231	        """Load the primary label file matching a video path by its stem."""
232	        path = LABELS_DIR / f"{Path(video).stem}.json"
233	        if not path.exists():
234	            raise FileNotFoundError(
235	                f"No label file at {path}. Label the fight in the Annotate "
236	                f"page, finish labeling, then create one with:\n"
237	                f"  python -m eval.cli export {video}"
238	            )
239	        return cls.load(path)
240	
241	    @classmethod
242	    def passes_for_video(cls, video: str | Path) -> list["FightLabels"]:
243	        """Every label file for a video: the primary `labels/<stem>.json` plus
244	        any `labels/<stem>.<labeler>.json` second passes (see plan 0e —
245	        double-labelling one round to measure an agreement ceiling)."""
246	        stem = Path(video).stem
247	        primary = LABELS_DIR / f"{stem}.json"
248	        extra = sorted(p for p in LABELS_DIR.glob(f"{stem}.*.json"))
249	        paths = ([primary] if primary.exists() else []) + extra
250	        return [cls.load(p) for p in paths]
251	
252	    def save(self, path: str | Path | None = None) -> Path:
253	        path = Path(path) if path else LABELS_DIR / f"{Path(self.video).stem}.json"
254	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
255	        self.strikes.sort(key=lambda s: s.frame)
256	        self.states.sort(key=lambda s: s.start)
257	        self.rounds.sort(key=lambda r: r.start)
258	        self.excluded.sort(key=lambda e: e.start)
259	        self.takedowns.sort(key=lambda t: t.frame)
260	        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
261	            json.dump(asdict(self), f, indent=2)
262	        return path
263	
264	    # -- validation --------------------------------------------------------
265	
266	    def validate(self) -> None:
267	        errs: list[str] = []
268	
269	        if self.fps <= 0:
270	            errs.append(f"fps must be positive, got {self.fps}")
271	
272	        for i, s in enumerate(self.strikes):
273	            if s.frame < 1:
274	                errs.append(f"strikes[{i}]: frame {s.frame} is not 1-based")
275	            if s.fighter not in FIGHTERS:
276	                errs.append(f"strikes[{i}]: fighter {s.fighter!r} not in {FIGHTERS}")
277	            if s.family not in FAMILIES:
278	                errs.append(f"strikes[{i}]: family {s.family!r} not in {FAMILIES}")
279	            if s.target not in TARGETS:
280	                errs.append(f"strikes[{i}]: target {s.target!r} not in {TARGETS}")
281	
282	        for i, t in enumerate(self.takedowns):
283	            if t.frame < 1:
284	                errs.append(f"takedowns[{i}]: frame {t.frame} is not 1-based")
285	            if t.fighter not in FIGHTERS:
286	                errs.append(f"takedowns[{i}]: fighter {t.fighter!r} not in {FIGHTERS}")
287	
288	        for i, s in enumerate(self.states):
289	            if s.state not in STATES:
290	                errs.append(f"states[{i}]: state {s.state!r} not in {STATES}")
291	            if s.end < s.start:
292	                errs.append(f"states[{i}]: end {s.end} before start {s.start}")
293	
294	        # State spans must not overlap — state_at() would be ambiguous.
295	        ordered = sorted(self.states, key=lambda s: s.start)
296	        for a, b in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
297	            if b.start <= a.end:
298	                errs.append(
299	                    f"state spans overlap: [{a.start},{a.end}] and [{b.start},{b.end}]"
300	                )
301	
302	        for i, r in enumerate(self.rounds):
303	            if r.end < r.start:
304	                errs.append(f"rounds[{i}]: end {r.end} before start {r.start}")
305	
306	        for i, c in enumerate(self.corner_swaps):
307	            if c.end < c.start:
308	                errs.append(f"corner_swaps[{i}]: end {c.end} before start {c.start}")
309	
310	        if errs:
311	            raise LabelError(
312	                f"{len(errs)} problem(s) in labels for {self.video}:\n  "
313	                + "\n  ".join(errs)
314	            )
315	
316	    # -- summary -----------------------------------------------------------
317	
318	    def summary(self) -> str:
319	        scored = len(self.scored_frames())
320	        mins = scored / self.fps / 60 if self.fps else 0
321	        by_family: dict[str, int] = {}
322	        for s in self.strikes:
323	            by_family[s.family] = by_family.get(s.family, 0) + 1
324	        fam = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(by_family.items()))
325	        landed = sum(1 for s in self.strikes if s.landed)
326	        return (
327	            f"{self.video}: {len(self.strikes)} strikes ({landed} landed) over "
328	            f"{mins:.1f} min of scored footage\n"
329	            f"  rounds={len(self.rounds)} state_spans={len(self.states)} "
330	            f"excluded={len(self.excluded)} takedowns={len(self.takedowns)}\n"
331	            f"  families: {fam or '(none)'}"
332	        )

1	"""Scoring: pipeline predictions vs. hand-labelled ground truth.
2	
3	Design notes
4	------------
5	**Strike matching ignores the fighter.** Predictions are matched to ground truth
6	on time proximity alone, then attribution accuracy is reported separately. This
7	deliberately separates two failure modes that a joint match key would conflate:
8	"we missed the strike entirely" and "we saw the strike but credited the wrong
9	corner". Corner assignment is a known weak point, and folding it into the
10	detection score would hide detection progress behind attribution noise.
11	Use ``strict_fighter=True`` to require the corner to match.
12	
13	**Corner read-back is not corner correctness.** ``fighter_accuracy`` compares
14	the labeller's corner against the pipeline's — but the labeller *picks* a corner
15	by clicking the box the overlay draws from ``fighter_frames.corner``, i.e. the
16	pipeline's own assignment. A tracker identity swap is therefore copied into the
17	label and cancels out here: the number reads near-100% however badly
18	``assign_corners`` swaps, and measures only whether the human read the box
19	correctly. It is circular in the same way seeded ``round`` spans are. The
20	non-circular measurement of corner correctness is the labeller's ``corner_swap``
21	spans (see ``corner_swap_check``); never quote this figure as an attribution
22	accuracy. The field keeps its name so existing baseline JSON stays comparable.
23	
24	**Only scored frames count.** Both ground-truth and predicted events outside a
25	labelled round, or inside an ``excluded`` span (replay, walkout, camera cut),
26	are dropped before matching rather than counted as false positives — the
27	pipeline should not be graded on footage nobody labelled.
28	
29	**Non-specific predictions are excluded from family/target denominators.** The
30	pipeline emits ``clinch_punch`` / ``ground_punch`` with no family or target, so
31	scoring those against a labelled ``hook``/``head`` would penalise it for a
32	distinction it never attempts. They still count for event-level detection.
33	"""
34	
35	import statistics
36	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
37	from typing import Optional
38	
39	import numpy as np
40	from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment
41	
42	from .predictions import PredictedStrike, Predictions
43	from .schema import STATES, FightLabels, Strike

48	@dataclass
49	class PRF:
50	    tp: int = 0
51	    fp: int = 0
52	    fn: int = 0
53	
54	    @property
55	    def precision(self) -> float:
56	        return self.tp / (self.tp + self.fp) if (self.tp + self.fp) else 0.0
57	
58	    @property
59	    def recall(self) -> float:
60	        return self.tp / (self.tp + self.fn) if (self.tp + self.fn) else 0.0
61	
62	    @property
63	    def f1(self) -> float:
64	        p, r = self.precision, self.recall
65	        return 2 * p * r / (p + r) if (p + r) else 0.0
66	
67	
68	@dataclass
69	class StrikeScore:
70	    detection: PRF = field(default_factory=PRF)
71	    tolerance_frames: int = 0
72	    # Accuracy numerators/denominators over matched pairs only.
73	    fighter_correct: int = 0
74	    fighter_total: int = 0
75	    family_correct: int = 0
76	    family_total: int = 0
77	    target_correct: int = 0
78	    target_total: int = 0
79	    landed_correct: int = 0
80	    landed_total: int = 0
81	    nonspecific_matches: int = 0
82	    family_confusion: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = field(default_factory=dict)
83	    # Signed (pred.frame - truth.frame) per matched pair, not absolute. A
84	    # systematic lag (e.g. labeller reaction time) is a bias to subtract once,
85	    # not spread to widen the tolerance window by — see bias/jitter below.
86	    matched_offsets: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
87	    missed: list[Strike] = field(default_factory=list)
88	    spurious: list[PredictedStrike] = field(default_factory=list)
89	
90	    def _acc(self, num: int, den: int) -> Optional[float]:
91	        return num / den if den else None
92	
93	    @property
94	    def offset_bias(self) -> Optional[float]:
95	        """Median signed offset — a systematic lag, not spread."""
96	        return statistics.median(self.matched_offsets) if self.matched_offsets else None
97	
98	    @property
99	    def offset_jitter(self) -> Optional[float]:
100	        """Median absolute offset — genuine temporal spread."""
101	        return statistics.median(abs(o) for o in self.matched_offsets) if self.matched_offsets else None
102	
103	    @property
104	    def fighter_accuracy(self) -> Optional[float]:
105	        return self._acc(self.fighter_correct, self.fighter_total)
106	
107	    @property
108	    def family_accuracy(self) -> Optional[float]:
109	        return self._acc(self.family_correct, self.family_total)
110	
111	    @property
112	    def target_accuracy(self) -> Optional[float]:
113	        return self._acc(self.target_correct, self.target_total)
114	
115	    @property
116	    def landed_accuracy(self) -> Optional[float]:
117	        return self._acc(self.landed_correct, self.landed_total)

123	    frames_correct: int = 0

125	    gt_transitions_per_min: float = 0.0
126	    pred_transitions_per_min: float = 0.0
127	    gt_median_dwell_secs: float = 0.0
128	    pred_median_dwell_secs: float = 0.0

152	        yields a healthy mean IoU, since the largest predicted segment overlaps

169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	# Strike matching
171	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
172	
173	def _match_strikes(
174	    gt: list[Strike],
175	    pred: list[PredictedStrike],
176	    tolerance_frames: int,
177	    strict_fighter: bool,
178	) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], list[int], list[int]]:
179	    """Optimal one-to-one matching minimising total temporal offset.
180	
181	    Greedy nearest-match is order-dependent and inflates or deflates the score
182	    depending on which end you start from, so this solves the assignment problem
183	    properly. Pairs beyond the tolerance are forbidden and dropped after solving.
184	
185	    Returns (pairs, unmatched_gt_indices, unmatched_pred_indices).
186	    """
187	    if not gt or not pred:
188	        return [], list(range(len(gt))), list(range(len(pred)))
189	
190	    big = tolerance_frames * 10 + 1_000_000
191	    cost = np.full((len(gt), len(pred)), float(big))
192	    for i, g in enumerate(gt):
193	        for j, p in enumerate(pred):
194	            offset = abs(g.frame - p.frame)
195	            if offset > tolerance_frames:
196	                continue
197	            if strict_fighter and g.fighter != p.fighter:
198	                continue
199	            cost[i, j] = offset
200	
201	    rows, cols = linear_sum_assignment(cost)
202	
203	    pairs = [(int(i), int(j)) for i, j in zip(rows, cols) if cost[i, j] < big]
204	    matched_gt = {i for i, _ in pairs}
205	    matched_pred = {j for _, j in pairs}
206	    return (
207	        pairs,
208	        [i for i in range(len(gt)) if i not in matched_gt],
209	        [j for j in range(len(pred)) if j not in matched_pred],
210	    )
211	
212	
213	def score_strikes(
214	    labels: FightLabels,
215	    preds: Predictions,
216	    tolerance_secs: float = DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS,
217	    strict_fighter: bool = False,
218	) -> StrikeScore:
219	    scored = labels.scored_frames()
220	    gt = [s for s in labels.strikes if s.frame in scored]
221	    pred = [s for s in preds.strikes if s.frame in scored]
222	
223	    tol = max(1, round(tolerance_secs * labels.fps))
224	    pairs, unmatched_gt, unmatched_pred = _match_strikes(gt, pred, tol, strict_fighter)
225	
226	    out = StrikeScore(tolerance_frames=tol)
227	    out.detection = PRF(tp=len(pairs), fp=len(unmatched_pred), fn=len(unmatched_gt))
228	    out.missed = [gt[i] for i in unmatched_gt]
229	    out.spurious = [pred[j] for j in unmatched_pred]
230	
231	    for i, j in pairs:
232	        g, p = gt[i], pred[j]
233	        out.matched_offsets.append(p.frame - g.frame)
234	
235	        out.fighter_total += 1
236	        if g.fighter == p.fighter:
237	            out.fighter_correct += 1
238	
239	        if not p.is_specific:
240	            # Grappling prediction — carries no family/target claim to grade.
241	            out.nonspecific_matches += 1
242	        else:
243	            out.family_total += 1
244	            if g.family == p.family:
245	                out.family_correct += 1
246	            key = (g.family, p.family)
247	            out.family_confusion[key] = out.family_confusion.get(key, 0) + 1
248	
249	            if g.target != "unknown":
250	                out.target_total += 1
251	                if g.target == p.target:
252	                    out.target_correct += 1
253	
254	        if g.landed is not None and p.landed is not None:
255	            out.landed_total += 1
256	            if g.landed == p.landed:
257	                out.landed_correct += 1
258	
259	    return out
260

265	
266	def _segments_from_frames(frames: list[int], state_of) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
267	    """Collapse a frame sequence into (state, length) runs, ignoring gaps."""
268	    segments: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
269	    for f in frames:
270	        s = state_of(f)
271	        if s is None:
272	            continue
273	        if segments and segments[-1][0] == s:
274	            segments[-1] = (s, segments[-1][1] + 1)
275	        else:
276	            segments.append((s, 1))
277	    return segments
278	
279	
280	def score_state(labels: FightLabels, preds: Predictions) -> StateScore:
281	    scored = sorted(labels.scored_frames())
282	    out = StateScore()
283	
284	    for f in scored:
285	        g = labels.state_at(f)
286	        if g is None:
287	            continue          # frame inside a round but not state-labelled
288	        p = preds.state_at(f)
289	        if p is None:
290	            # `preds` is sometimes a second FightLabels (agreement — see
291	            # cli.py's `agreement` command), whose state_at() returns None
292	            # outside a labelled span, unlike Predictions.state_at() which
293	            # always falls back to initial_state. Either way, "no prediction
294	            # here" is not a mismatch to grade.
295	            continue
296	        out.frames_scored += 1
297	        if g == p:
298	            out.frames_correct += 1
299	        out.confusion[(g, p)] = out.confusion.get((g, p), 0) + 1
300	
301	    minutes = len(scored) / labels.fps / 60 if labels.fps else 0
302	    gt_segs = _segments_from_frames(scored, labels.state_at)
303	    pred_segs = _segments_from_frames(scored, preds.state_at)
304	
305	    if minutes:
306	        out.gt_transitions_per_min = max(0, len(gt_segs) - 1) / minutes
307	        out.pred_transitions_per_min = max(0, len(pred_segs) - 1) / minutes
308	    if gt_segs:
309	        out.gt_median_dwell_secs = statistics.median(n for _, n in gt_segs) / labels.fps
310	    if pred_segs:
311	        out.pred_median_dwell_secs = statistics.median(n for _, n in pred_segs) / labels.fps
312	
313	    return out
314

317	# Rounds

319	
320	def score_rounds(labels: FightLabels, preds: Predictions) -> RoundScore:
321	    out = RoundScore(gt_count=len(labels.rounds), pred_count=len(preds.rounds))
322	
323	    for g in labels.rounds:
324	        best, best_iou = None, 0.0
325	        for p in preds.rounds:
326	            inter = max(0, min(g.end, p.end) - max(g.start, p.start) + 1)
327	            union = g.length + p.length - inter
328	            iou = inter / union if union else 0.0
329	            if iou > best_iou:
330	                best, best_iou = p, iou
331	        if best is not None:
332	            out.matched.append((
333	                g.round,
334	                best_iou,
335	                (best.start - g.start) / labels.fps,
336	                (best.end - g.end) / labels.fps,
337	            ))
338	
339	    return out

342	def score(
343	    labels: FightLabels,
344	    preds: Predictions,
345	    tolerance_secs: float = DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SECS,
346	    strict_fighter: bool = False,
347	) -> Report:

349	        print(f"  warning: label fps ({labels.fps}) != pipeline fps ({preds.fps}); "
350	              f"using label fps for all conversions")
351	    return Report(
352	        video=labels.video,
353	        fps=labels.fps,
354	        scored_minutes=len(labels.scored_frames()) / labels.fps / 60,
355	        strikes=score_strikes(labels, preds, tolerance_secs, strict_fighter),
356	        state=score_state(labels, preds),

381	    add(f"  ground truth {d.tp + d.fn:4d}   predicted {d.tp + d.fp:4d}")
382	    add(f"  TP {d.tp:4d}   FP {d.fp:4d}   FN {d.fn:4d}")
383	    add(f"  precision {d.precision:6.1%}   recall {d.recall:6.1%}   F1 {d.f1:6.1%}")
384	    if s.matched_offsets:
385	        add(f"  temporal offset on matches: bias {s.offset_bias:+.1f}f "
386	            f"(systematic lag)   jitter {s.offset_jitter:.1f}f (spread)")
387	
388	    add("\nCLASSIFICATION   (matched strikes only)")
389	    add(f"  corner read-back    {_pct(s.fighter_accuracy)}  ({s.fighter_total} matches)")
390	    add(f"  strike family       {_pct(s.family_accuracy)}  ({s.family_total} specific)")
391	    add(f"  target zone         {_pct(s.target_accuracy)}  ({s.target_total} specific)")
392	    add(f"  landed vs missed    {_pct(s.landed_accuracy)}  ({s.landed_total} confirmable)")
393	    add("  NB read-back is not attribution accuracy: the labeller reads the corner")
394	    add("     off the pipeline's own overlay, so a swap is copied into the label and")
395	    add("     cancels out. Measure corner correctness with corner_swap spans.")
396	    if s.nonspecific_matches:
397	        add(f"  {s.nonspecific_matches} matches were grappling predictions "
398	            f"(no family/target claim — excluded above)")
399	
400	    if s.family_confusion:
401	        add("\n  family confusion (truth → predicted):")
402	        for (g, p), n in sorted(s.family_confusion.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]:
403	            mark = "  " if g == p else " ✗"
404	            add(f"   {mark} {g:>9} → {p:<9} {n:4d}")
405	
406	    st = r.state
407	    add(f"\nFIGHT STATE")
408	    add(f"  per-frame accuracy {_pct(st.accuracy)}  ({st.frames_scored} frames scored)")
409	    add(f"  transitions/min    truth {st.gt_transitions_per_min:6.1f}   "
410	        f"predicted {st.pred_transitions_per_min:6.1f}")
411	    add(f"  median dwell (s)   truth {st.gt_median_dwell_secs:6.2f}   "
412	        f"predicted {st.pred_median_dwell_secs:6.2f}")
413	    if st.pred_transitions_per_min > 3 * max(st.gt_transitions_per_min, 0.1):
414	        add("  ⚠ predicted state flaps far faster than reality — hysteresis is "
415	            "not holding.")
416	    if st.confusion:
417	        add("\n  state confusion (truth → predicted):")
418	        labels_seen = sorted({p for _, p in st.confusion})
419	        add("           " + "".join(f"{p:>10}" for p in labels_seen))
420	        for g in STATES:
421	            row = [st.confusion.get((g, p), 0) for p in labels_seen]
422	            if any(row):
423	                add(f"  {g:>8} " + "".join(f"{n:>10d}" for n in row))
424	
425	    rd = r.rounds
426	    verdict = "OK" if rd.count_correct else "WRONG"
427	    add(f"\nROUNDS   truth {rd.gt_count}   predicted {rd.pred_count}   count {verdict}")
428	    for num, iou, dstart, dend in rd.matched:
429	        add(f"  round {num}: IoU {iou:5.1%}   start {dstart:+6.2f}s   end {dend:+6.2f}s")
430	    if not rd.count_correct:
431	        add("  NOTE: mean IoU stays high when one round is split into several — "
432	            "the count is what catches that.")
433	
434	    if show_examples and s.missed:
435	        add(f"\nWORST MISSES (first {show_examples} of {len(s.missed)} FN)")
436	        for m in s.missed[:show_examples]:
437	            t = m.frame / r.fps
438	            add(f"  f{m.frame:<6d} {int(t // 60):d}:{t % 60:05.2f}  "
439	                f"{m.fighter:<4} {m.family}_{m.target}")
440	
441	    if show_examples and s.spurious:
442	        add(f"\nWORST FALSE POSITIVES (first {show_examples} of {len(s.spurious)} FP)")
443	        for m in s.spurious[:show_examples]:
444	            t = m.frame / r.fps
445	            # `m` is a plain Strike (no `.action`) when `preds` is a second
446	            # FightLabels, i.e. scoring an agreement run rather than pipeline
447	            # predictions — see cli.py's `agreement` command.
448	            action = getattr(m, "action", f"{m.family}_{m.target}")
449	            add(f"  f{m.frame:<6d} {int(t // 60):d}:{t % 60:05.2f}  "
450	                f"{m.fighter:<4} {action}")
451	
452	    add("")
453	    return "\n".join(L)
454

90	## Analysis Player Layout
91	
92	`Player.tsx` implements a cinematic, full-page layout with five stacked sections (top → bottom):
93	
94	1. **Top grid** (`1fr 410px`, collapses single-column below 1100px) — `<VideoPlayer>` + `FighterOverlay` + ROUND chip on the left; `LiveFeed` filling the right column via absolute positioning so it always matches the video column height.
95	2. **FIGHT STATISTICS** — `FightStatistics.tsx`: glass bar with `monitoring` icon + `ScopeToggle` (Whole Fight / Round 1 / Round 2); two `FighterColumn` cards below (real scope state selects the mock stat set from `fightMock.ts`).
96	3. **MOMENTUM** — `Momentum.tsx`: `PaceChart` (SVG area/line, mock pace data, real time-axis from `currentTime`/`duration`; real `r1EndSeconds` from `useRounds` or fallback mock).
97	4. **MATCHUP** — `MatchupCard.tsx`: tale-of-the-tape header + `EdgeRow` needles for Height/Reach/Age + Recent Form W/L chips.

99	### Live feed event derivation
100	`LiveFeed` drives on **real** backend events (same `useEvents` hook). Each `Event.description` is classified by `deriveEventCat()` in `eventMeta.ts` using the same strike/ground regexes that existed before in `Player.tsx` and `EventFeed.tsx`. Filter pills (All / Strikes / Fight State / Grapple) and click-to-seek work the same way as the design reference.
101	
102	### Mock data
103	All hardcoded values (fighter profiles, per-round stats, pace arrays, recent form) live in `src/mocks/fightMock.ts`. Every gap is documented with the API shape needed to replace it in `TODO_BACKEND_DATA.md`.
104	
105	### Responsive
106	`useWindowWidth()` drives a `narrow = width < 1100` flag. Below 1100px: top grid collapses to single column (live feed becomes a fixed-height `420px` block below controls); fighter columns stack; matchup tale-of-the-tape collapses; form lists both align left.
107	
108	## API Proxy (vite.config.ts)
109	Both `/events` and `/fights` are proxied to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
110	Video files are served from `public/` via a custom range-request middleware.
111	
112	## Frame-numbering contract
113	**Frames are 1-based** — the first frame of the video is frame 1.
114	
115	Convert `video.currentTime` to a frame number with:
116	```ts
117	const currentFrame = Math.floor(currentTime * fps) + 1;
118	```
119	where `fps` comes from `FightResponse.fps` (an integer stored on the `fights` DB row).
120	
121	This value is used to:
122	- Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` in `FighterOverlay`
123	- Filter `events.filter(e => e.frame <= currentFrame)` in `Player`
124	- Match round boundaries: `rounds.find(r => currentFrame >= r.start_frame && currentFrame <= r.end_frame)`
125	
126	Never hardcode an fps value — always use `selectedFight.fps`.
127	
128	## FighterOverlay component
129	`<canvas>` absolutely positioned over the video (`pointer-events: none`).
130	
131	On each `currentFrame` change:
132	1. Resize canvas to its CSS display size (`canvas.width = canvas.clientWidth`, etc.)
133	2. Clear canvas
134	3. If `showBoxes` is false, return early
135	4. Look up `frameMap.get(currentFrame)` → array of `FighterFrame`
136	5. Scale each bbox from the fight's **native resolution** (`fightWidth` × `fightHeight` from `FightResponse`) to the canvas display size:
137	   ```ts
138	   const scaleX = canvas.width / fightWidth;
139	   const scaleY = canvas.height / fightHeight;
140	   ```
141	6. Draw red rect for `corner === 0`, blue for `corner === 1`
142	
143	`VideoPlayer` accepts `children` so `FighterOverlay` can be rendered inside the `position: relative` video container and stack correctly.
144	
145	## Fight selector (Player.tsx)
146	- Populated from `useFights`, filtered to `isFightViewable(state)` (`completed` or `labeling_complete`)
147	- Defaults to the most recently processed fight (last element of the list)
148	- Changing selection re-fetches events, frames, and rounds for the new fight
149	
150	## Deleting a fight
151	`DELETE /fights/{id}` is irreversible — it kills any running pipeline, unlinks the video file, and
152	cascades away predictions, label events/spans, rounds and fighter frames. Two entry points, both
153	routed through `ConfirmDialog`:
154	
155	- **`Player.tsx`** — Delete button in the back-nav row (icon-only when `narrow`). The only way to
156	  delete a healthy fight. Two things the handler must keep doing: `videoRef.current.pause()` before
157	  the request, because the DELETE unlinks the file the `<video>` is streaming and the
158	  `requestVideoFrameCallback` loop is still reading it; and `navigate('/', { replace: true })`, so
159	  browser Back can't land on a now-dead `/fights/{id}`.
160	- **`Annotate.tsx`** — icon-only button at the far right of the header, past "Finish Labeling".
161	  Its `confirmDelete` state is mirrored into `confirmDeleteRef` and checked in the global keydown
162	  handler alongside `endOpenRef` — **any new modal on this page must do the same**, or its overlay
163	  will happily sit there while `z`/`o`/`p`/digit presses keep writing label events and spans
164	  underneath it.
165	- **`FightList.tsx`** — gated behind `errored` (`failed || invalid`), so it does *not* appear on
166	  healthy cards; it's a "delete and re-upload" recovery affordance, not a general delete. One
167	  dialog instance lives outside the `.map`, driven by `pendingDelete`.
168	
169	Set `KEEP_VIDEO_ON_DELETE=1` on the backend when exercising this by hand — the row still goes, but
170	the source video survives.
171	
172	## Key design decisions
173	- `useFighterFrames` builds a `Map<number, FighterFrame[]>` on load for O(1) per-frame overlay lookup during playback
174	- `useRounds` provides DB-backed round boundaries; `Player` uses `rounds.find(...)` instead of a hardcoded duration constant
175	- `stepFrame(delta)` uses `delta / fps` seconds, so frame-stepping is always exact regardless of the video's actual fps
176	
177	## Labelling (Annotate page)
178	
179	`Annotate.tsx` (`/fights/{id}/annotate`) is where a **manual**-mode upload gets hand-labelled once it reaches `labeling_in_progress`. It shares `AnnotateStage`/`VideoPlayer`/`FighterOverlay` with the Player, but reads/writes **only** `label_events`/`label_spans` — never `fight_events` (pipeline predictions), so re-running the AI pipeline over a labelled fight can never destroy the labels.
180	
181	**Palette-driven strikes/state/etc. (`taxonomy.ts` → `label_events`).** Every `ToolItem` in `TOOL_GROUPS` drives its palette button, keyboard shortcut, and the keyboard legend from one definition. Hand strikes (jab/hooks/uppercuts/elbow) carry `hasTarget: true` — plain key = head, `Shift`+key = body, read via `e.code` (not `e.key`, which a US layout maps to a different character under Shift) together with `e.shiftKey`. Kicks carry a `fixedTarget` instead (the action name already encodes it: `calf_kick`/`low_kick` → leg, `middle_kick` → body, `high_kick` → head). `successForAction` returns `null` for every strike except `knockdown` — landed-vs-missed is deferred, so nothing claims a strike landed by default.
182	
183	**Span annotation (`O`/`P` keys → `label_spans`).** `round`/`corner_swap`/`excluded` spans share one table with a `kind` column. `round` spans are auto-seeded server-side from the AI-segmented `rounds` table on first `GET /label-spans/` and rendered as draggable blocks in `AnnotationTimeline`'s ROUNDS lane (edge-drag calls `onUpdateSpan`). `corner_swap`/`excluded` are start/end toggles: `Annotate.tsx`'s `openSpanRef` tracks the in-flight span id per kind so the second `O`/`P` press knows what to close — `toggleSpan()` creates a span with `end_frame=null` on open, `PUT`s `end_frame` to close it. `AnnotationTimeline` renders an open span dashed, running to the current playhead.
184	
185	**"Finish Labeling" is gated.** `POST /fights/{id}/finish-labeling` (via `handleFinishLabeling`) 409s until every detected round has a confirmed `round` label-span — the backend check (`rounds_fully_annotated`), not anything client-side.
186	
187	**Fight-state marks are change points, not spans.** `W`/`F`/`G` (STRIKING/CLINCH/GROUND) log a single-frame `label_event`; `AnnotationTimeline`'s STATE lane derives contiguous segments by pairing each mark with the next one chronologically (last mark implicitly runs to the end of the timeline in the UI — the harness-side derivation in `ai/eval/labels_db.py` instead runs it to the end of its round, which matters when exporting).

164	def _print_agreement_ceiling(video: str, tolerance_frames: int) -> None:
165	    """`labels/<stem>.agreement.json`, if present, caps how good a score can
166	    honestly be — an F1 above it is fitting label noise, not detecting
167	    strikes better than a second human would. Only meaningful when it was
168	    measured at the same tolerance as this run (plan 0f)."""
169	    path = LABELS_DIR / f"{Path(video).stem}.agreement.json"
170	    if not path.exists():
171	        return
172	    from .report_io import load_report_json
173	    raw = load_report_json(path)
174	    agreement_tol = raw.get("tolerance_frames")
175	    if agreement_tol != tolerance_frames:
176	        print(f"\n  (human agreement ceiling in {path.name} was measured at "
177	              f"±{agreement_tol}f, not ±{tolerance_frames}f for this run — "
178	              f"not comparable, skipping)")
179	        return
180	    d = raw["report"]["strikes"]["detection"]
181	    tp, fp, fn = d["tp"], d["fp"], d["fn"]
182	    p = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
183	    r = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0
184	    f1 = 2 * p * r / (p + r) if (p + r) else 0.0
185	    print(f"\n  human agreement ceiling: F1 {f1:.1%}  (from {path.name})")
